# Clipboard Saver

> A macOS `NSServices` app that writes the clipboard to a file from the Finder
> context menu, converting HTML or RTF to Markdown. No window, no Dock icon; it
> terminates after each save. Repository: github.com/nyimbi/clip_saver.

## What it does

Reads the richest representation on the general pasteboard, converts it to
Markdown, derives a filename from the document's own heading, and writes one
file per destination folder. The filename is offered in an `NSSavePanel` and
stays editable. Writes are atomic and never overwrite.

## Repository shape

The git repository is the inner `Clipboard_saver/` directory, which contains the
Xcode project. A parent directory holds two superseded artifacts that are NOT
in the repository and NOT built: `save_clipboard.py` (dead 35-line Python
prototype) and `QuickAction/save_clipboard_md.sh` (working 450-line zsh Quick
Action with different behaviour — no HTML conversion, appends to `.md`, no save
panel).

## Build and test

- `xcodebuild -project Clipboard_saver.xcodeproj -scheme Clipboard_saver -destination 'platform=macOS' test`
- Current status: **126 tests, 0 failures** (123 unit, 3 UI). Clean Release build with zero
  warnings from project sources (the single warning emitted is from Xcode's
  `appintentsmetadataprocessor` toolchain step).
- Target: macOS 15.5+, Swift 5 language mode, bundle id `datacraft.Clipboard-saver`.
- Deployment copies to `/Applications/Clipboard_saver.app`. It must be launched
  once after install so it registers itself as a login item.

## Source files

### `Clipboard_saver/Clipboard_saverApp.swift` (~322 lines)

The services provider and save pipeline.

- `@main Clipboard_saverApp` — declares only `Settings { EmptyView() }`; there is
  no window by design. `LSUIElement` in the plist keeps it out of the Dock.
- `AppDelegate` — `NSApplicationDelegate` conforming to `NSServicesProvider`.
  - `applicationDidFinishLaunching` sets `NSApp.servicesProvider = self`, calls
    `NSUpdateDynamicServices()`, then `registerAtLoginIfNeeded()`.
  - `registerAtLoginIfNeeded()` calls `SMAppService.mainApp.register()` unless
    the status is already `.enabled`. **This is load-bearing**: Finder only lists
    the services while the provider process is running, and nothing else
    launches a Services-only app, so without a login item the tool is invisible
    after every reboot.
  - `run(_:userData:error:)` — "Save Clipboard to File", from the Services menu
    of any app. Destination is the Desktop.
  - `saveToFolder(_:userData:error:)` — right-clicked folder(s) or file(s).
    Reads file URLs from the service pasteboard; the clipboard *content* comes
    from `NSPasteboard.general`.
  - `saveHere(_:userData:error:)` — background of a Finder window. Resolves the
    folder via an `NSAppleScript` `tell application "Finder"` call. This is the
    only service Finder offers on a background right-click.
  - `saveInteractively(pasteboard:into:reveal:error:)` — reads the clipboard,
    computes a suggested name, shows the save panel, then writes. Modal on
    purpose: the process terminates on return, so an async panel would be killed
    before the user answered it.
  - `askForFilename(suggesting:in:)` — `NSSavePanel.runModal()` seeded with the
    derived name. The typed value is re-sanitised (the field accepts anything,
    including path separators) and a missing extension is restored.
  - `save(pasteboard:into:)` / `save(export:into:name:)` — the write path,
    returning `SaveOutcome` (`.written` / `.cancelled` / `.failed`) rather than
    terminating. This split is what makes the pipeline testable in-process.
  - `resolveDestinations(from:frontWindowFolder:)` — selection first, front
    Finder window as fallback.
  - `destinationFolders(from:)` — a selected folder is used directly; a selected
    file contributes its parent. De-duplicates. `public.file-url` first, then
    the legacy `NSFilenamesPboardType`.
  - `finish(_:reveal:_:)` — a non-nil `error` pointer makes macOS show an
    alert; nil completes silently. Cancelling is not an error.

### `Clipboard_saver/MarkdownExporter.swift` (90 lines)

Chooses the representation. `enum MarkdownSource` carries the extension policy:
`.markdown`/`.html`/`.rtf` → `.md`, `.plain` → `.txt`.

Precedence in `export(from:)`: plain text that is already Markdown → HTML →
RTF → plain. Plain Markdown winning over HTML is deliberate; see
`looksLikeMarkdown`.

`looksLikeMarkdown` matches a combined `NSRegularExpression` of block syntax
(ATX heading, fence, list marker, blockquote, table row, thematic break,
setext underline). Any single hit counts. The previous rule required three list
lines *or* a heading *and* a list, so a ChatGPT answer that was a heading
followed by prose was classified plain and saved as `.txt`.

### `Clipboard_saver/HTMLToMarkdown.swift` (1133 lines)

The bulk of the code. A single-pass byte-level tokenizer over the UTF-8 bytes
of the HTML, building a small `Element`/`Node` tree, then rendering to Markdown
chunks.

- `parse(_:)` — tokenizer. Handles comments, doctype, start/end tags, void
  elements, quoted and unquoted attribute values, and entity decoding
  (`decodeEntities`, ~60 named entities plus numeric).
  - `static let maximumDepth = 256`. **Load-bearing.** `Element` is a recursive
    value type, so 50,000 unclosed `<div>` tags built a 50,000-deep tree whose
    release recursed 50,000 frames and killed the process with SIGSEGV. Past the
    ceiling elements are not pushed; their content attaches to the innermost
    element that was kept.
  - Unterminated attribute quote rewinds rather than consuming to end of input —
    a truncated pasteboard would otherwise lose the entire document body.
  - `implicitClosures` closes an open `li`/`p`/`tr`/`td` on a new one, so sloppy
    markup does not nest items inside their predecessors.
  - `ignoredElements` (script, style, svg, form, …) skips to the matching close
    tag; text is discarded while skipping.
- `render(_:)` — walks the tree into `Chunk` values (heading, paragraph, quote,
  code, listItem, rule, table).
- List identity: each `<ul>`/`<ol>` gets an id and an *ancestry* chain
  (`ListFrame.ancestry`). `belongsToSameList(as:after:)` treats two items as the
  same list when one ancestry is a prefix of the other. This is what keeps a
  nested list tight against its parent while keeping two sibling lists apart —
  an `<ol>` followed by a `<ul>` needs a blank line or they fuse into one list.
- `join(_:)` — separator logic (blank line vs single newline) plus fence
  widening: `fenceLength(for:)` counts the longest backtick run *anywhere* in
  the block, so content containing ``` still renders.
- `escapeInline` escapes `\ ` `` ` `` `*` `[` `]` `<` `>`. `escapeLineStart`
  escapes leading `#`, `>`, `~`, `-`, `+`, `=` and ordered-list markers —
  escaping the marker itself (`1\.`) rather than the digit, since `\1.` would
  not prevent an ordered list.
- `normalize(_:)` collapses HTML whitespace runs to a single space but
  *preserves* leading/trailing space, so `Hello <b>world</b> ok` does not fuse to
  `Hello **world**ok`. `collapse` trims.
- Style inference for `style="font-weight:700"` / `font-style:italic` /
  `monospace` / `line-through`, because Safari emits styled spans rather than
  `<b>`/`<i>`.

### `Clipboard_saver/RTFToMarkdown.swift` (343 lines)

Fallback for RTF-only pasteboards. RTF has no tag tree, so structure comes from
the style run.

- `modalFontSize(_:)` — the most common font size is body text, ties going to
  the smaller. **Load-bearing.** The previous thresholds mapped anything between
  11 and 15.5pt to heading level 5, and the system body size is 13pt, so every
  paragraph of prose came out as `##### text`.
- `rankHeadingSizes(_:bodySize:)` — only sizes clearly larger than the body
  *and* bold become headings, ranked to levels 1…6.
- `bullet(_:)` — finds the marker after leading whitespace, because
  `NSAttributedString` pads bullets with tabs. Returns a `Bullet` struct with
  the text after the marker. `isListBody` rejects a body containing a tab or
  empty, which is what separates `"\t1\tFirst"` (a list item) from `"1\t2\t3"`
  (a three-column row).
- `renderTable(_:)` — column count is the *mode* of cell counts across the
  block. The previous divisor search could not tell a 2×3 table from a 3×2 one.

### `Clipboard_saver/FilenameGenerator.swift` (159 lines)

- `title(from:)` — first non-empty line, preferring an ATX heading (closing
  hashes stripped) or a setext underline. `clipboard_save_<timestamp>` fallback.
- `resolveCollision(_:in:)` — appends ` (n)` until free, bounded at 9,999.
- `String.sanitizedForFilename` — removes `[/:*?"<>|\]`, collapses whitespace,
  truncates to 80 chars **on a word boundary**, strips trailing separators (so
  `Just a sentence.` does not become `Just a sentence..txt`), strips leading
  dots, and escapes reserved device names.
- `String.sanitizedForTypedFilename` — the same cleaning but no 80-char cut,
  because silently shortening a name a person just typed is worse than a long
  filename. Only the 240-byte APFS component limit applies.

### `Clipboard_saver/Info.plist`

Declares the three services plus the bundle identity keys. `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE`
is `NO` for this target, so `CFBundleIdentifier`, `CFBundleExecutable`,
`CFBundlePackageType`, `CFBundleShortVersionString` and `CFBundleVersion` are
**declared here explicitly** — omitting them means LaunchServices cannot
register the app and the service never appears.

- `LSUIElement` = true (agent app, no Dock icon).
- `NSServices`: `run` (accepts `NSStringPboardType`, `public.html`, `public.rtf`
  — the last two are what let the Services-menu path convert rich content at all),
  `saveToFolder` (accepts `NSFilenamesPboardType`, `public.file-url`),
  `saveHere` (no `NSSendTypes`, therefore offered unconditionally).
- Both Finder services carry `NSRequiredContext` = `com.apple.finder`.

### `Clipboard_saver/Clipboard_saver.entitlements`

`com.apple.security.app-sandbox` = false. Writing to arbitrary folders and
sending AppleEvents to Finder both require it.

## Test files

### `Clipboard_saverTests/HTMLToMarkdownTests.swift` (52 tests)

Structure preservation per construct, escaping, task lists, tables, entities,
and hostile input: 200k unclosed tags, 100k balanced, 5k nested lists, 100k
unbalanced closes, malformed entity soup, unterminated attribute quote, plus
`testLargeDocumentConvertsQuickly` (63 KB under 5 s — ~300× headroom over the
real 15 ms) as a guard against reintroducing super-linear behaviour.

### `Clipboard_saverTests/ServiceContractTests.swift` (13 tests)

Asserts the `Info.plist` ↔ runtime contract that fails *silently* otherwise:
`CFBundleIdentifier`/`CFBundleExecutable`/`CFBundlePackageType` present and
correct; exactly three services; every `NSMessage` resolves to a real
`…:userData:error:` selector on `AppDelegate` (enumerated via
`class_copyMethodList`); `NSPortName` equals the executable; the background
service is unconstrained while the folder service requires a file selection;
`NSAppleEventsUsageDescription` is present.

### `Clipboard_saverTests/SavePipelineTests.swift` (14 tests)

Pasteboard → file on disk, extension selection, repeated saves not overwriting,
one file per destination, empty/missing/non-directory destinations reported
rather than crashed, and destination resolution including the background
fallback.

### `Clipboard_saverTests/FilenameGeneratorTests.swift` (15 tests)

Heading, trailing-hash, setext and first-line title extraction; illegal
characters, newlines, control characters, leading dots, reserved names,
word-boundary truncation, Unicode preservation; sequential collision suffixes.

### `Clipboard_saverTests/ChosenFilenameTests.swift` (10 tests)

The name confirmed in the save panel is used verbatim; the first destination
may replace, additional destinations are collision-resolved; typed names are
sanitised but not shortened to the readability limit.

### `Clipboard_saverTests/MarkdownExporterTests.swift` (9 tests)

Representation precedence against synthetic multi-type pasteboards, plus the
Markdown-detection table.

### `Clipboard_saverTests/RTFToMarkdownTests.swift` (10 tests)

Body prose is not a heading, large bold text is, monospace fences, tab-prefixed
bullets, ordered bullets, indented block quotes, tab-delimited tables, ragged
row padding, three-column non-transposition.

### `Clipboard_saverUITests/` (3 tests)

Untouched Xcode templates — a launch smoke test and a launch-performance
measurement. They assert nothing about this app.

## Defects found and fixed

All four were invisible to the build, and the first two were invisible to code
review as well.

1. **No bundle identity.** `CFBundleIdentifier` and `CFBundleExecutable` were
   absent. LaunchServices cannot register or launch a Services app without an
   identifier, so the context menu never offered the service. No build error.
2. **Services invisible unless the provider is running.** Finder only lists them
   while the process is alive; nothing launched a Services-only app, so after a
   reboot the tool was gone until opened by hand. Fixed with a login item.
3. **Test suite did not compile** (`ClipboardManagerTests.swift:83`, unhandled
   `try`), so nothing had ever been verified, and over half the tests asserted
   on `AppDelegate.defaultFileName` — a method with no call site, alongside
   `ContentView.swift`, which was never in any `Scene` and so compiled but never
   ran.
4. **The converter destroyed the document.** Round-tripping HTML through
   `NSAttributedString` and re-deriving structure from font metrics lost
   paragraphs (became `#####`), lists (`"\t•\tItem"`), tables, blockquotes and
   link targets.

Plus two found by fuzzing the parser afterwards:

5. **SIGSEGV on deep nesting** — recursive `Element` deallocation, capped at 256.
6. **Content loss on a truncated pasteboard** — unterminated attribute quote.

One change was made and reverted after testing: collapsing `saveToFolder` and
`saveHere` into a single service. It looked like a duplicate-menu-entry
cleanup, but Finder supplies no file URL on a background right-click, so
`saveToFolder` is not offered there and removing `saveHere` removed the only way
to save into the current folder.

## Known limitations

- `saveToFolder` (right-click a folder) is unit-tested and appears in the real
  context menu, but was not isolated in an end-to-end GUI run. The background
  `saveHere` path was.
- The `NSFilenamesPboardType` fallback branch is defensive and untestable —
  that pasteboard type cannot be synthesised.
- The app icon asset catalog is empty; Finder shows a generic icon.
- The UI test target asserts nothing meaningful.
- No licence file.
